editorial:
Imagine being stuck on a long train ride with a bunch of people who all knew the same person, but they don't necessarily like each other. That is the setup here. You follow a group of friends and former lovers traveling to a funeral for an artist. The vibe is heavy and awkward, but in a way that keeps you interested. As the train rolls along, people start talking about things they should have kept secret. Old flames start sparking again, and you realize that almost everyone in the group is hiding something or wanting someone they can't have. It feels like a pressure cooker where emotions just keep building up until they boil over.

What really makes this work is the acting. You can feel the tension in every look and silence. The pacing is a bit slow, which might bore some people, but it helps you feel the weight of the grief and the longing. It is a great pick if you love character studies and messy human relationships. Since it is an older film, you should definitely try to find it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or rent it on Apple TV to get the best picture. If you love owning physical media, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your collection is a smart move for the quality.
endingExplained: At the end, the group arrives at the family home and the emotional walls finally break. After the burial, the characters face the truth about their failed romances and regrets. Instead of a happy ending, you get a realistic look at loss. Some characters find a small bit of peace, while others realize they will never get back what they lost. It wraps up by showing that grief brings people together, even if they stay broken.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep character dramas and stories about complicated love.
